notes: In the relative clause 'asher bo mum the verbless possessive preposition carries hath under rule 43 and the suffix is unrepresented, the written relative having supplied the English subject.

he that hath a flat nose stays whole with charum because no other morpheme stands in that item at all: dropping hath diminishes the participle's own rendering, which is not the case in LEV.21.20, where every other morpheme of the clause keeps its own English.
